originalTitle: US Open tennis 2026: Alcaraz faces Faria, Sabalenka cruises and more on day four – live
summary: Join our writers for all the action at Flushing Meadows, with home hopes the biggest names in action on day four
content: Carlos Alcaraz put up a good fight to try for the match’s first break, but Jaime Faria held through the 14-point game to keep the first set even. That’s a big hold, despite two double faults. We’re only through two rounds, but Stefanos Tsitsipas is having himself a nice US Open. He started with an upset of No 10 seed Arthur Fils in the first round and has followed it up tonight by taking down Lloyd Harris 6-7 (1-7), 6-3, 7-6 (7-4), 6-4. The Greek man is into a grand slam third round for the first time since Roland Garros 2024 and the US Open third round for the first time in five years. Tsitsipas’s backhand finally looks to be working again, and he’s fun to watch when he’s locked in. Carlos Alcaraz holds in both of his service games and it’s 2-1 to start. He didn’t drop a point in either of those games, and his serve is looking good so far: he’s averaging a speed of 109mph and won the third game with an ace. Tiafoe Update: the American finally got a well-earned break in the second set and is up 6-5. This second set has been tighter than the first, but if he can hold serve against Rei Sakamoto, he’ll have a comfortable at two sets to love. Carlos Alcaraz is in the same brown basketball-inspired kit for this match. It’s almost time for Carlos Alcaraz v Jaime Faria at Ashe. Alcaraz looked good on Monday in his first match after four months away with a wrist injury. The Spaniard said he was “pain-free” in his opener, a 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 win over Roman Safiullin. We’ll see if he can continue that play tonight. An area to watch will be his serve. He kept his serves at a low speed – just as he had in the mixed doubles with Serena Williams last week – averaging just 113mph behind his first serve. No 18 seed Jiri Lehecka has beaten Toby Samuel in straight sets 6-4, 6-2, 6-4. The 23-year-old Brit was looking to reach the third round of a grand slam for the first time but falls short. Lehecka, a quarter-finalist in New York last year, will face either Lloyd Harris or Stefanos Tsitsipas. That match is a good one right now: Tsitsipas is up two sets to one, having pulled out the third in a tiebreak. Frances Tiafoe and Rei Sakamoto are locked in a tight second set on Armstrong. “It’s always the best atmosphere,” Aryna Sabalenka tells the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd after her win. “I’m happy with the level I played today, happy with the focus.” She’ll face Kamilla Rakhimova of Uzbekistan in the third round. We thought Karolina Muchova’s 6-1, 6-0 battering of Katie Boulter in 58 minutes would be the most dominant match we’d see today. This one may take the edge. World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka made quick work of qualifier Polina Iatcenko, needing just 53 minutes. It’s one of Sabalenka’s quickest matches this year: per Tennis Abstract, it’s just the third match in 2026 she has played that lasted less than an hour. Iatcenko, in her first year playing in the main draw, didn’t offer much of a threat, and Sabalenka dominated with 24 winners, three aces and eight of 11 net points won. She still had some moments of frustration; both players finished with 16 unforced errors. But Sabalenka gets a quick, confident win – the kind she’s been looking for amid a choppy stretch of play since her spring double at Indian Wells and Miami – and her win streak at the US Open improves to 16 straight matches. Aryna Sabalenka lets her service game go to deuce, but responds with an emphatic forehand winner and then watches Polina Iatcenko’s return land long. She’ll have a chance to break Iatchenko for the match. Three unforced errors in a row for Aryna Sabalenka gave Polina Iatcenko the break at 1-3, but Sabalenka returned with a few ruthless winners to break her right back. Aryna Sabalenka is rolling. Have you heard that already? Polina Iatcenko is looking a bit overwhelmed, down 0-3 in the second set. She has five unforced errors this set. Sabalenka will serve to try to go up 4-0. Tiafoe Alert: the American won the first set 6-3. Polina Iatcenko got on the board and earned a nice applause from the Ashe crowd, but Aryna Sabalenka held her serve and took the set 6-1. The world No 1 is moving fast: the first set took just 24 minutes. She isn’t letting Iatcenko play any long rallies, and she’s come up to the net after her serve on several points to win with volleys. Sabalenka is 29-2 when she wins the first set at the US Open. She let Camila Osorio climb back into the match during the second set of their first-rounder, so we’ll see if anything similar plays out tonight, but she’s looked dominant thus far. Elsewhere, Frances Tiafoe is up 5-2 on Rei Sakamoto. Their fifth game went to six deuces and 18 points before a pair of unforced errors ruined Sakamoto’s chance for a break. Aryna Sabalenka is rolling. She’s up 5-0 in the first. Twelve winners, 23 points won. That’s a nice win for Denis Shapovalov to set up a third-round meeting with Ben Shelton. The Canadian was up 5-1 in the third set before letting Luca Van Assche climb back into the match and force a tiebreak. The final was 6-0, 6-4, 7-6 (9-7). In the women’s draw, rising American star Iva Jovic beat Magdalena Fręch 7-5, 6-3. Jovic will face Brit Francesca Jones in the second round. With that, the longest first round in US Open history is over. Opponents of Aryna Sabalenka can watch their matches snowball quickly if they give up an early break. Polina Iatcenko may be the latest to learn that tonight. Sabalenka is up 3-0 after just 11 minutes. She delivered a 106mph serve for the hold. After having his tournament opener against Andrea Guerrieri postponed until day four, Alex de Minaur had to endure another two-hour rain delay before putting away the Italian qualifier in straight sets. No orange for Sabalenka tonight! She’s opted for the black Nike set instead. After a rainy two days at Flushing Meadows, the roof at Arthur Ashe Stadium is open for tonight’s matches.
